definitions.gloss: exposition; statement of one's argument; written discussion
definitions.explanation: The act of presenting and developing an argument or viewpoint in a systematic, logical manner, typically in writing. Often used in academic and examination contexts.

examples.japanese: {論述|ろんじゅつ}{試験|しけん}の{準備|じゅんび}をする。
examples.english: To prepare for an essay exam.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}の{考|かんが}えを{論理的|ろんりてき}に{論述|ろんじゅつ}する{力|ちから}が{求|もと}められる。
examples.english: The ability to present your ideas logically is required.

examples.japanese: この{課題|かだい}では、{賛成|さんせい}か{反対|はんたい}かの{立場|たちば}を{明確|めいかく}にして{論述|ろんじゅつ}してください。
examples.english: For this assignment, please clearly state your position for or against and present your argument.

notes: Used with する to form {論述|ろんじゅつ}する (to expound, to present an argument). Common collocations: {論述|ろんじゅつ}{試験|しけん} (essay exam), {論述|ろんじゅつ}{問題|もんだい} (essay question), {論述|ろんじゅつ}{式|しき} (essay-type format). Primarily found in academic and examination settings. Related: {論文|ろんぶん} (thesis, academic paper — the finished product), {記述|きじゅつ} (description — broader, not necessarily argumentative), {論証|ろんしょう} (demonstration, proof — focuses on proving a point).
